summary: Deployed inventory-api as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine 3.23) with kernel OOM protection (oom_score_adj=-1000 via a start_post hook), verified it kept serving through a real global-OOM event that instead killed a dedicated memory-hog test process, and completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol.
actions_performed: Installed python3 on node1 via apk (no python3/httpd was present)
Created dedicated system user/group inventoryapi and app at /opt/inventory-api/app.py (Python HTTP server on :8080 with /health and /inventory endpoints)
Created OpenRC init script /etc/init.d/inventory-api running the app as inventoryapi, with a start_post hook that sets oom_score_adj=-1000 on the running pid
Enabled (rc-update add default) and started the service; fixed a log-permission issue and verified startup
Verified service health and oom_score_adj via curl and /proc before inducing OOM
Wrote /opt/mem-hog/hog.py, a memory-hog test tool with default oom_score_adj=0, launched via setsid+nohup so it survived the exec session

Drove the hog to consume RAM until the kernel's global OOM killer fired; dmesg confirms pid 3438 (python3 hog, oom_score_adj:0) was killed while inventory-api (pid 3273, oom_score_adj:-1000) was untouched
Confirmed inventory-api continued serving /health and /inventory uninterrupted (same pid, incrementing uptime) throughout and after the OOM event
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline, then rebooted node1 via `reboot` with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled until node1 was reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (7045e228-89a9-419a-82af-119f6363505f -> 1a5c0035-16be-4f4d-92b9-a2134a982ec8) and uptime showed 'up 0 min'
Verified post-reboot recovery: inventory-api auto-started with a new pid, oom_score_adj=-1000 reapplied by the start_post hook, and /health and /inventory responded correctly

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
evidence.summary: rc-service inventory-api status shows 'started', enabled in rc-update default runlevel, curl to /health and /inventory succeed

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is protected from the OOM killer (oom_score_adj=-1000)
evidence.summary: cat /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj returns -1000 immediately after start and again just before the OOM event; dmesg OOM dump lists pid 3273 python3 with oom_score_adj -1000

evidence.requirement: A memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory and is the one the kernel stops
evidence.summary: hog.py launched (pid 3438, oom_score_adj 0) consumed RAM until free memory was exhausted; dmesg shows kernel's global OOM killer selected and killed pid 3438 (anon-rss ~1.8GB, oom_score_adj:0), not inventory-api

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving during/after the OOM event
evidence.summary: After the hog was OOM-killed, inventory-api (pid 3273) was confirmed alive in the same dmesg task listing and curl to /health returned 200 with the same pid and increasing uptime, with no restart

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: pre-restart baseline (boot identity + service health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7045e228-89a9-419a-82af-119f6363505f and confirmed inventory-api started, pid 3273, oom_score_adj -1000, health/inventory endpoints responding

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `reboot` via setsid+disown; exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the connection dropped on the next call

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: proof of changed boot identity (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id read as 1a5c0035-16be-4f4d-92b9-a2134a982ec8, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, with `uptime` showing 'up 0 min'

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of service, OOM protection, and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventory-api auto-started under rc-update default (new pid 2314), oom_score_adj re-applied to -1000 by the start_post hook, and curl to /health and /inventory returned correct data
